policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere עֲלָךְ and ketiv עליך are two spellings of the same 2ms suffixed form 'to thee'; ASV 'to thee' renders either identically and no textual note is mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback retained.

Qere אֶחָךְ and ketiv אחיך are orthographic variants of 'thy brethren' with the same 2ms suffix; ASV 'thy brethren' renders either identically and no textual note is mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback retained.

Qere דָּאיְנִין and ketiv דאנין are plene/defective spellings of the same plural 'judges'; ASV 'judges' renders either identically and no textual note is mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback retained.

Qere לִשְׁרֹשִׁי and ketiv לשרשו are spelling variants of the same infinitive 'rooting out'; ASV 'banishment' renders either identically. The verse note 'Aramaic rooting out' is classed other and glosses the shared root's meaning, not a reading. Base qere fallback retained.
